SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - JANUARY 27, 2020 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
JANUARY 27, 2020, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Joshua Merigala, Bible Mission Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Recreation Services Division Students in
  Leadership Training/BASES Program participants Cameron Lacorte and TJ
  Jiramanatnakon.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  Cerritos Special Olympics C Division Boys and Girls Soccer Team – Cerritos Heat (Special
  Olympics Southern California Fall Games Gold Medal recipients).

  Valley Christian High School Girls Volleyball Team (CIF Champions).

5A.1. An informational update on the Tuesday, March 3, 2020 Cerritos General Municipal
  Election and Measure C.

  An informational update on on the Tuesday, March 3, 2020 Cerritos General Municipal
  Election and Measure C was presented by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer and Ryan
  Carey, Finance Manager.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Case Van Der Linden spoke in opposition of Measure C.

  Sue Carter spoke in support of Measure C.

  Martin Grossman spoke in opposition of Measure C.

  Gail Grossman spoke in opposition of Measure C.

  Mel Cortez stated he would support Measure C if the City began budget cuts.

  Raymond Kim spoke in opposition of Measure C.
 City of Cerritos  January 27, 2020

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Coleen Aldrich spoke in opposition of Measure C.

  Jay Gray spoke regarding Council benefits and in opposition of Measure C.

  Rocky Pavone spoke regarding his candidacy for City Council and in opposition of
  Measure C.

  Daisy spoke in opposition of Measure C.

  Anantha Ramachandran requested a long-range plan for revenues if Measure C is
  passed by the voters.

  Gary Aldrich suggested reevaluating the City's management structure rather than
  raise revenues through a sales tax.

  Jane Yim expressed concerns regarding a recent interaction between a
  Councilmember and a resident.

  Sam Desai expressed concerns regarding a recent interaction between a
  Councilmember and a resident.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke regarding his years as a Cerritos resident and the
  upcoming election.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  January 9, 2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of January 9, 2020
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated January 27, 2020
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register
  of Demands, as follows:

  City of Cerritos  1/27/2020  $4,390,493.85 (COUNCIL)
 City of Cerritos  January 27, 2020

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.1. (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 4-0, with one
  Commissioner absent, to approve the following:

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING PRECISE PLAN 71-27(2019) AMENDMENT, A
  PROPOSAL BY AMERICA'S TIRE ON BEHALF OF THE PROPERTY OWNERS TO
  REMODEL THE INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR OF THE EXISTING TIRE STORE BUILDING
  AND PERFORM RELATED SITE AND LANDSCAPE IMPROVEMENTS AT 11524 SOUTH
  STREET, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS ZONED
  REGIONAL COMMERCIAL (CR) (APN 7039-021-022) (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Sandy Cisneros, Senior Planner. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments. Noting there were no
  individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments and the public
  hearing.

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to waive full
  reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2020-03, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS APPROVING PRECISE PLAN 71-27(2019) AMENDMENT, A
  PROPOSAL BY AMERICA'S TIRE ON BEHALF OF THE PROPERTY OWNERS TO
  REMODEL THE INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR OF THE EXISTING TIRE STORE
  BUILDING AND PERFORM RELATED SITE AND LANDSCAPE IMPROVEMENTS
  AT 11524 SOUTH STREET, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT
  PROPERTY IS ZONED REGIONAL COMMERCIAL (CR) (APN 7039-021-022)
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract to IDS Group, Inc. for professional
  design services for the boiler replacement, roof improvements, and bulkhead
  replacement at the Cerritos Swim & Fitness Center (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Amend the contract to IDS Group, Inc. in the amount of $36,830 for developing
  construction documents and performing project management services for the boiler
  replacement at the Cerritos Swim & Fitness Center; and

  2. Amend the contract to IDS Group, Inc. in the amount of $58,194 for developing
  construction documents and performing project management services for the roof
  improvements at the Cerritos Swim & Fitness Center; and

  3. Amend the contract to IDS Group, Inc. in the amount of $6,800 for developing
  performance specifications for the bulkhead replacement at the Cerritos Swim &
  Fitness Center; and

  4. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract modifications
  that may be necessary to complete the specified scope of work (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  January 27, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  Review and consideration to reject the sole bid for fire alarm system replacement at
  the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts, Project No. 12716, Bid No. 1394-19, and
  to authorize the City to negotiate a contract (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Reject the sole bid received for the replacement of the fire alarm system at the
  Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts; and

  2. Find that, due to the unique nature of the facility and scheduling complexities
  involved in completing the proposed work, and the high degree of specialized and
  technical skill required to complete the work, it is in the best interest of the City to
  dispense with competitive bidding; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to negotiate with contractors in the open
  market a proposal to replace the fire alarm system at the Cerritos Center for the
  Performing Arts pursuant to the design and specifications (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of an application to seek Los Angeles County Safe, Clean
  Water Program (Measure W) funding for a regional stormwater capture project at the
  Cerritos Sports Complex (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Mike O’Grady, Environmental Services Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Direct staff to proceed with an application for Los Angeles County Measure W funding
  for a regional stormwater capture project at the Cerritos Sports Complex; and

  2. Report back to the Cerritos City Council for further direction if and when funding is
  allocated for the project (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  January 27, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  Review and consideration by the Cerritos City Council of potential modifications to
  or deletion of the City’s designated truck route along Shoemaker Avenue between
  Alondra Boulevard and 166th Street adopted by Urgency Ordinance No. 1030
  (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water
  & Power, Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager, and Dario Simoes, Assistant City
  Engineer. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  John Briquelet, Whitney High School Principal, spoke regarding concerns
  expressed by students and parents related to the truck route on Shoemaker
  Avenue.

  John Moran expressed concerns regarding truck route directional signage.

  Sophia Tse expressed concerns regarding pedestrian safety as related to truck
  traffic.

  Anantha Ramachandran expressed support to remove the truck route on
  Shoemaker Avenue and Artesia.

  Jennifer Hong expressed support to remove the truck route on Shoemaker
  Avenue and requested more thorough study on the item.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to direct staff to
  present an Ordinance to the City Council de-classifying Shoemaker Avenue, between
  Alondra Boulevard and 166th Street, as a designated truck route (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.
 City of Cerritos  January 27, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 7

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  CONSENSUS (Solanki): Directed the City Manager to place an informational item
  on the next agenda related to the City Council benefits package.

  Reports on this item were continued to the meeting of February 13, 2020.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 11:44 p.m.
